text:
## Outcome

I preserve J. The proposed successor (a "level-relation target" added to P7's taxonomy, with the global-availability interval relabelled "under the independence assumption") rests on a reading of P9 that the supplied criticism does not establish, and the criticism's own best case — that P7's list is non-exhaustive and the snapshot-as-a-whole target can absorb the compatibility worry — is a re-description, not a defect in J's organization. Because the substantive reason the criticism offers for change is one J's own retreat clause anticipates, the warranted move is not to construct a successor but to state what the objection does and does not reach.

The relevant protected distinction is P7's: criticising a rule differs from criticising a record, and further from criticising a booking history, a snapshot, or an assumption. The criticism treats the compatibility worry as failing to land on the rule target and therefore as needing a new target. That inference does not hold: P7's target list is open-ended by its own wording ("One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, …"), and the snapshot-as-a-whole entry is broad enough to cover a naming defect the snapshot carries — an unnamed shared resource that would decide cross-booking compatibility is a property of the snapshot, reported by the snapshot, and its absence is a snapshot-level gap in the same general shape as P7's third illustration (logical time behind an expected expiry). The rule "take min/max per booking" can be accepted as locally correct while this snapshot-level gap remains; that is exactly the separation P7 already provides, without a new target.

The criticism's own defence of the addition is conditional: it says the addition stands only if a case is supplied where the compatibility worry is not absorbable by "criticize the snapshot as a whole" and not reducible to the time-assumption or rule targets. It then notes it has not supplied such a case. That is the retreat clause's outcome: the addition is not warranted by the material on hand.

What remains, and is not settled here: P7 does not claim exhaustiveness, so a level-relation target is not ruled out; the criticism's reading of P9's "invisible" as merely marking a conditional premise is compatible with an alternative reading in which P9 already treats the compatibility worry as a snapshot-internal naming gap; and the criticism itself proposes rather than establishes the defect. Nor is the criticism's treatment of the E009 record settled — the record diagnoses the locus as a WHL expressiveness limitation and proposes (without installing) a resource model or possible-worlds set, while J's construct proposes reinterpretation without language extension. Those are competing diagnoses of the same passage; the criticism's point that J's phrasing blurs the competition is a fair observation about exposition, not a reason to change J's organization.

On the operator's question — whether the P9 objection requires a change to an account of global availability, and if so what in P7's sense is being questioned — J's answer stands: the objection, to the extent it lands, is a snapshot-level criticism of what the interval is claimed to summarise, not a rule-level or record-level one, and not a new target. No account change is forced, and no language extension is installed or required. The separately attributed E009 record remains an unendorsed prior occurrence; its proposed repairs remain proposals, not components of the frozen carrier, and nothing in this reasoning installs them. No executability, bearing, or standing is claimed for anything above; the frozen parent material, the E009 occurrence, the selected carrier, and the construct and criticize occurrences remain distinct historical records with their original provenance and no standing effect.
